findings.title: Hardcoded credential: aws access key id
findings.description: A value matching the `aws-access-key-id` pattern was found committed in source. Secrets in version control are exposed to everyone with repository access and remain in history even after removal.
findings.why_vulnerable: A credential is committed in source, so anyone with repository access (or a leaked copy) obtains it.
findings.attacker_perspective: Read the value straight from version control history and use it directly against the corresponding service.
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized access to the associated account or service, and any data or spend it controls.

remediation.summary: Remove the secret from source and rotate it.
remediation.guidance:
1. Revoke/rotate the exposed credential now, assume it is compromised.
2. Move the value to a secret manager or an environment variable loaded at runtime.
3. Purge it from git history (e.g. git-filter-repo) so it is not recoverable.
4. Add a pre-commit secret scan to prevent recurrence.

findings.title: Attack chain: injection foothold beside an exposed credential
findings.description:
This component contains both a hardcoded credential and an injection vulnerability. An attacker exploiting the injection gains code or query execution in the very component that holds the secret, so a single foothold yields both execution and a credential for lateral movement.

Chained findings: secrets.aws-access-key-id (app.py:2); patterns.python-shell-true (app.py:4)
findings.why_vulnerable: This component contains both a hardcoded credential and an injection vulnerability. An attacker exploiting the injection gains code or query execution in the very component that holds the secret, so a single foothold yields both execution and a credential for lateral movement.
findings.attacker_perspective: Individually these findings look moderate; chained, each one enables the next, so an attacker can walk the entire path from untrusted input to impact.
findings.business_impact: Compounded impact: the chain reaches a materially worse outcome than any single finding in it.

remediation.summary: Break the chain: fixing any one link stops this path, fix all for defense in depth.
remediation.guidance: Breaking the weakest link is enough to stop this specific path, but address every chained finding so a variant cannot re-open it.

findings.title: Unsafe yaml.load without SafeLoader
findings.description: yaml.load with the default loader can construct arbitrary Python objects from the document.
findings.why_vulnerable: yaml.load with the default loader can construct arbitrary Python objects from the document.
findings.attacker_perspective: Feed a YAML payload using `!!python/object/apply` tags to execute code.

findings.title: Command execution with shell=True
findings.description: Running a subprocess through the shell lets shell metacharacters in any interpolated input execute additional commands.
findings.why_vulnerable: Running a subprocess through the shell lets shell metacharacters in any interpolated input execute additional commands.
findings.attacker_perspective: Provide input containing `; rm -rf /` or `$(...)` to run arbitrary commands as the app user.
findings.business_impact: Remote code execution on the host.

remediation.summary: Pass the command as an argument list without shell=True, and validate/escape any external input.
remediation.guidance: Pass the command as an argument list without shell=True, and validate/escape any external input.

findings.title: Weak hash algorithm (MD5/SHA1)
findings.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes (collisions, speed) and must not be used for integrity or password hashing.
findings.why_vulnerable: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes (collisions, speed) and must not be used for integrity or password hashing.
findings.attacker_perspective: Exploit collision weaknesses, or brute-force fast hashes for stored passwords.
findings.business_impact: Forged signatures/integrity checks, or recovered passwords.

remediation.summary: Use SHA-256+ for integrity and a slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2) for passwords.
remediation.guidance: Use SHA-256+ for integrity and a slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2) for passwords.
